newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Plane crash casts shadow on Brazil bolsa, ends off.
newsitem.headline: Plane crash casts shadow on Brazil bolsa, ends off.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed lower in light turnover as trading slowed after an airplane, carrying bank and company executives, crashed in Sao Paulo early Thursday, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active stocks ended off 0.15 percent at 65,332 points. Volume totalled 257 million reais ($250.1 million).
"The accident stopped the market. We were shocked," said a broker.
The Fokker-100 aircraft from Brazil's TAM airline slammed into homes in a densely populated area of Sao Paulo, killing all 95 on board and eight people on the ground.
The Rio de Janeiro-bound flight crashed shortly after take-off at 0820 local time/1020 GMT, the time of day when many executives travel between Brazil's financial centers.
Even a Central Bank decision to allow foreign investors to buy debentures convertible into shares under the Annex Four regulations for non-Brazilian investments failed to enliven trade.
"The measure was good, but the timing wasn't," said a trader, referring to the fact that the plane crash held investor attention today.
Annex Four regulates foreign investment in Brazilian stocks, debentures and privatization bonds.
The Central Bank also decided to cut a tax charged on banks borrowing abroad for re-lending to the domestic market.
Preferred shares of Brazilian TAM airline plunged following the accident. The company's stock dropped 22.28 percent, closing at 50.52 reais after falling to 48 reais.
Bellwether Telebras preferred fell 0.39 percent to 76.30 reais.
